Skip next section Jharkhand student protests: Police use water cannons to disperse marching students 08/10/2026 August 10, 2026 Jharkhand student protests: Police use water cannons to disperse marching students The sit-in protest in Jharkhand began on July 25 following allegations of irregularities in government recruitment examinations Image: ANI Video Grab Police used tear gas, batons and water cannons to disperse the crowd of students marching towards the state assembly in Ranchi in the eastern state of Jharkhand on Monday, reports said. On Sunday, the sixth round of talks between student protesters and the government failed to reach a breakthrough after students alleged irregularities in government recruitment exams. The sit-in protests in Jharkhand began on July 25. Students are demanding the cancellation of recruitment examinations citing irregularities Image: ANI Video Grab Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto has been on an indefinite hunger strike since August 2 is demanding action over alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC), Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level (JSSC CGL) and other competitive examinations required to qualify for government jobs. Meanwhile, authorities on Monday arrested former Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) chairperson L Khiangte in connection with alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, reports said. The protest witnessed heavy police deployment across state capital Ranchi Image: ANI Video Grab Earlier, Chief Minister Hemant Soren has assured the protesting students that his government would take action over alleged exam irregularities and invited them for talks. Female protesters lie down on the stage during a demonstration Image: Yousuf Sarfaraz/SOPA Images/ZUMA/picture alliance https://p.dw.com/p/5IY9u Skip next section Court calls sexual harassment allegations against former wrestling chief 'fabricated' 08/10/2026 August 10, 2026 Court calls sexual harassment allegations against former wrestling chief 'fabricated' A Delhi court called the sexual harassment allegations against former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh "false and fabricated" and part of a "deep conspiracy which seems to be politically motivated," media reports said. Singh was acquitted last week of the sexual harassment and stalking charges brought by female athletes. The former lawmaker from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), had denied allegations that he groped wrestlers and demanded sexual favors. In its detailed judgment, the court cited "material contradictions" in the wrestlers’ accounts, inconsistencies between their allegations and documentary evidence, and the absence of contemporaneous complaints, media reports said. The court said some allegations appeared "rehearsed, well-practiced and planted." Lawyer Rebecca John, who represented four of the women, described the acquittal as "deeply, deeply disturbing" on Monday, news channel NDTV reported. The allegations had triggered months of protests in New Delhi in 2023 , led by prominent Indian wrestlers with hundreds joining the sit-in demonstrations accusing authorities of failing to act against Singh. Delhi police charged Singh in 2023 , and a court formally brought charges against him in 2024 over allegations involving five women. The allegations surfaced in April-May 2023 when women wrestlers protested at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, accusing the former WFI of sexually harassing women wrestlers [FILE: April 18, 2024] Image: Shrikant Singh/Hindustan Times/Sipa USA/picture alliance https://p.dw.com/p/5IXoc Skip next section Rhiya Ahir speaks out after online abuse over protest 08/10/2026 August 10, 2026 Rhiya Ahir speaks out after online abuse over protest Shalu Yadav Ahir’s act of defiance, standing in front of a police van carrying protesters during last month’s CJP-led demonstrations, brought her widespread attention [FILE: July 22, 2026] Image: Ashish Vaishnav/AP Photo/picture alliance Mumbai-based model Rhiya Ahir, who gained attention after standing in front of a police van carrying protesters during last month's Cockroach Janta Party-led demonstrations , has spoken about facing online abuse and threats following the protest. In an interview with DW's Shalu Yadav, Ahir said the attention had come at a "heavy price" of online trolling and harassment, adding that women should be able to express their views without being targeted. She referred to comments made about women protesters, including comments that they "should be raped" and would "enjoy it," saying such remarks could influence others and should not be allowed to go unchallenged. "I read one comment saying 'we are going to rip you apart from the middle. And nobody's going to come to lay flowers on your grave,'" she said. Ahir described the attacks as "criminal." "I will not let it slide," she said. "I will not let them feel that they can sit behind their blank screens and feel so powerful by belittling other people. Her comments come amid a wider online campaign targeting women who took part in the CJP-led protests, with reports of fake and AI-manipulated images, doxxing and threats against participants. https://p.dw.com/p/5IXTQ Skip next section Right-wing commentator arrested over sexual assault remarks targeting protesters 08/10/2026 August 10, 2026 Right-wing commentator arrested over sexual assault remarks targeting protesters Right-wing accounts on social media are targeting the women at the CJP protests, reports say [FILE: July 25, 2026] Image: Sajjad Hussain/AFP An activist who considers himself a right-wing "political commentator" was arrested in the southern state of Kerala on Sunday over remarks he allegedly made about the women at the Cockroach Janta Party-led student protests last month, media reports said. The case was registered following a complaint alleging that videos on TG Mohandas' YouTube channel, Pathrika, were intended to disturb public order and create fear and unrest . According to reports, in the videos, Mohandas allegedly said the Delhi protests could lead to gang rape and claimed that women attending it "like rape" and that some "enjoy being raped." He also called for police to open fire at protesters. News channel NDTV reported that Mohandas is a former member of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the ideological parent of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). However, the RSS has denied any association with the commentator. The BJP on Monday criticized the arrest as "discriminatory" and accused the Kerala government of attempting to divert attention from other issues, reports said. Women protesters being targeted online The development comes amid an online campaign targeting women who took part in CJP-led student protests. The countrywide stir ended last month with the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Multiple reports indicate that young women involved in the movement are facing severe online harassment . They have been targeted with fake and AI-manipulated images, as well as a barrage of online abuse, including assault threats. Additionally, their phone numbers and home addresses have been leaked online alongside targeted attacks against their family members. https://p.dw.com/p/5IXKz Skip next section Welcome to our coverage 08/10/2026 August 10, 2026 Welcome to our coverage Shakeel Sobhan | Elizabeth Schumacher Editor Hello! This is Shakeel from DW's New Delhi Studio bringing you the latest updates from across India. Female protesters who took part in Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demonstrations against the government are facing harassment and doxxing. In the latest development, a right-wing activist was arrested in the southern state of Kerala for allegedly posting a video saying that those attending the protests "like rape." Meanwhile, a Delhi court has said allegations of sexual harassment made by women wrestlers against former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh were "false" and "fabricated." https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c78g.text: Image source, Swedish Coast Guard Image caption, Three of the four Nord Stream pipelines were ruptured by explosions in September 2022 By Jake Lapham Published 19 August 2026 A Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia on suspicion of taking part in the bombing of the Nord Stream gas pipelines between Russia and Germany. The suspect is alleged by German authorities to have been one of the scuba divers who planted explosives on the pipelines in September 2022, following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. He is the second man to be arrested over the plot, which has strained relations between Kyiv and Berlin - one of the key European backers for Ukraine's war effort. "The suspect participated in the necessary dives" for the sabotage, German prosecutors alleged, adding they were pursuing the suspect's extradition from Croatia. A journey to the site of the Nord Stream explosions Published 18 November 2022 Explosions, cyber attacks... welcome to hybrid warfare Published 6 February 2023 Prosecutors identified the man only as trained scuba diver Vladimir Z, however he is understood to be Volodymyr Zhuravlyov, who was arrested in Poland in 2025 over the undersea plot. In that case, a Polish judge refused a German extradition request, arguing that if Ukraine was responsible for the attack, then it was a "just" act. Zhuravlyov was then released, prompting a ripple of surprise from the crowd in court and a smile from the man in the dock. The other suspect in the case is former Ukrainian military officer Serhiy Kuznetsov. He was arrested in Italy in August 2025 and later extradited to Germany where he is set to face trial. He has denied responsibility for the explosions and appeared before a court in Hamburg in June. Prosecutors allege Kuznetsov led a team that used a yacht rented at Rostock in Germany to plant explosives on the pipelines close to the Danish Baltic Sea island of Bornholm. In a letter sent to the United Nations Security Council following the explosions, and reported by Reuters at the time, German investigators said "traces of subsea explosives were found in the samples taken from the boat". Although the Nord Stream 1 pipeline was in operation at the time, Nord Stream 2 had yet to go into service. After Zhuravlyov's planned extradition from Croatia, officials said he will be brought before an investigating judge to face charges of causing explosions and sabotage. Blame for the blasts, which crippled a long-controversial energy supply line from Russia to Germany, initially focused on Moscow until signs of Ukrainian involvement began to emerge. Officials in Kyiv have repeatedly denied any role . German courts have treated the destruction of Nord Stream 1 as falling within their jurisdiction because the pipelines end at Lubmin in the German state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Prosecutors have also alleged the pipelines' destruction affected the country's energy security and internal safety. Germany played a key role in the Nord Stream project, including providing technical expertise and political support ahead of its launch - which was attended by then Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011. Poland was always been a vocal critic of the pipeline project with Russia, arguing it made Berlin too dependent on Moscow. The route also deprived Poland of transit fees for the gas. Ukraine and the US were also longstanding opponents of the pipelines. The unharmed horse was eventually cornered by police, before being lassoed. Police officers followed and cornered the horse on motorbikes, before it was wrangled by a lasso-carrying cowboy. The horse was given a drink of water before being walked back to the start of the Desfile de la Gente parade, Santa Fe Police Department said in a post on Facebook. https://aa.com.tr/en/economy/turkish-def.text: #BREAKING With defense alliance established with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, Türkiye cementing solidarity and aiming to generate solutions to regional problems: Erdogan RSS Diary Anadolu Ajansı © 2026 Economy Türkiye Turkish defense giant Aselsan signs new export contract in Poland Aselsan agrees with Poland’s AMZ-Kutno on joint project for additional ARSUS reconnaissance, surveillance systems Mucahithan Avcioglu 08 September 2026 • Update : 08 September 2026 ISTANBUL Turkish defense company Aselsan signed a contract with Polish armored vehicle manufacturer AMZ-Kutno for a joint project involving additional ARSUS reconnaissance and surveillance systems. The agreement was signed during the MSPO 2026 International Defense Industry Exhibition in Poland, Aselsan said Tuesday on Turkish social media platform NSosyal. “We signed a contract at MSPO 2026 with Poland’s AMZ-Kutno for a joint project covering additional ARSUS reconnaissance and surveillance systems,” the company said. ASELSAN said it would continue expanding its operations and local partnerships in Poland through its advanced technological solutions, local office, ongoing projects and cooperation with Polish defense companies. Türkiye’s Secretariat of Defense Industries described the agreement as “a new export success for our defense industry in Poland.” “The cooperation between ASELSAN and AMZ-Kutno is an important example of our high-technology solutions finding concrete application in Poland’s defense projects,” it added. news_share news_share_description subscription_contact subscription contact_the_ombudsman is_there_an_error_in_this_story LATEST NEWS All US, Denmark, Greenland sign Arctic security agreement at UN General Assembly Trump says US to build 2 major military bases in Greenland Trump says he expects Iran deal after US midterm elections Italy, Iran discuss negotiations to reopen Strait of Hormuz Amnesty urges UEFA to suspend Israel, calls Nations League participation ‘unconscionable’ Canadian released by US immigration agency after 9 months in ‘hellhole’ US F-16 crashes at Spangdahlem air base in Germany See All Japan’s foreign reserves fall $79.6B after record yen intervention US closes $1.9B loan to restart Iowa nuclear plant
